audits.title: A clinical audit on the practice of platelet transfusions at a tertiary paediatric referral centre.
audits.standard: Criteria agreed by the audit committee
audits.setting: Paediatric Institute, Kuala Lumpur Hospital, tertiary paediatric referral centre

cycle1.period: One month prospective plus previous month retrospective

audits.other_findings: More detailed local clinical practice guidelines recommended.
audits.citation: Jamal R, Hoe TS, Ong LC, Afifah I, Khuzaiah R, Doraisamy G. A clinical audit on the practice of platelet transfusions at a tertiary paediatric referral centre. Malays J Pathol. 1998;20(1):35-40. PMID: 10879262.

audits.title: An audit of the use of platelet concentrates in the prophylaxis of thrombocytopenic haemorrhage in a large haematology unit.
audits.standard: Threshold platelet count for prophylactic transfusion of 20 x 10(9)/l
audits.setting: Large haematology unit, University College and Middlesex School of Medicine, London

cycle1.result: Lack of adherence to the threshold, with transfusions at higher platelet counts; major bleeding occurred above threshold when additional clinical factors present.

audits.intervention: A lower transfusion threshold was recommended and instituted.

cycle2.result: 20% reduction in use of platelet concentrates with no increase in major bleeding episodes.

audits.citation: Kelsey HC. An audit of the use of platelet concentrates in the prophylaxis of thrombocytopenic haemorrhage in a large haematology unit. Blood Coagul Fibrinolysis. 1992;3(5):647-649. doi:10.1097/00001721-199210000-00021. PMID: 1450333.

audits.title: A simple automatized audit system for following and managing practices of platelet and plasma transfusions in a neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Clinical justification of platelet and FFP transfusions based on pretransfusion platelet count and PT-% thresholds
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Hospital for Children and Adolescents, Helsinki University Central Hospital
audits.intervention: Automated audit system recording pretransfusion platelet count and prothrombin time, used for staff education and feedback.

cycle2.result: FFP transfusions with pretransfusion PT-% > 49%: 0.9%; no significant change in platelet transfusion practice.

audits.other_findings: Three periods of 120-152 days with 543 admissions; 60% of platelet transfusions above the count threshold (19% of all platelet transfusions) could not be clinically justified.
audits.citation: Petäjä J, Andersson S, Syrjälä M. A simple automatized audit system for following and managing practices of platelet and plasma transfusions in a neonatal intensive care unit. Transfus Med. 2004;14(4):281-288. doi:10.1111/j.0958-7578.2004.00515.x. PMID: 15285724.

audits.title: An audit of platelet transfusion within the Wellington Cancer Centre.
audits.standard: Local prophylactic platelet transfusion policy and international recommendations

cycle1.result: Decisions to withhold prophylactic platelets adhered to policy in 99%.

audits.other_findings: Breaches were mostly transfusion before the trigger was reached; multiple dose transfusions were almost never appropriate.
audits.citation: Buhrkuhl DC, Karlsson MK, Carter JM. An audit of platelet transfusion within the Wellington Cancer Centre. Intern Med J. 2012;42(1):65-70. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2010.02358.x. PMID: 21040321.

audits.title: Opportunities for improving platelet transfusion practice: A large retrospective audit across 22 hospitals.
audits.standard: Guideline thresholds: platelets below 100 × 10^9/L for neurosurgery, cardiac surgery or ECMO; below 50 × 10^9/L for procedures, bleeding or therapeutic anticoagulation; below 10 × 10^9/L otherwise (non-immune thrombocytopenia)
audits.setting: 22 hospitals, adult general medicine, subspecialty medicine and critical care admissions
audits.other_findings: Non-compliance was high with antiplatelet therapy (48.5%), cardiac surgery (49.7%) and primary prophylaxis (47.2%); academic hospitals had lower non-compliance than community hospitals (OR 0.768).
audits.citation: Ryan S, Liu Y, Raza S, Loeffler A, Relke N, Gabarin N, et al.. Opportunities for improving platelet transfusion practice: A large retrospective audit across 22 hospitals. Br J Haematol. 2026;208(2):670-682. doi:10.1111/bjh.70304. PMID: 41449709.

audits.title: An audit of platelet transfusion indications in acute leukaemia patients: six-year experience at an Academic Centre.
audits.standard: British Society for Haematology platelet transfusion guidelines
audits.setting: Academic tertiary centre, University Hospital Dr. Jose Eleuterio Gonzalez, Monterrey

cycle1.result: 75.3% of 745 platelet transfusion episodes in 154 patients were appropriate; Paediatrics 63.9% and Internal Medicine 86.8%; wards 82.3%.

audits.other_findings: Most inappropriate transfusions had a pre-transfusion count above 20×10^9/L without valid justification (45.1%).
audits.citation: Jaime-Pérez JC, García-Salas G, Turrubiates-Hernández GA, Alvarado-Navarro DM, Marfil-Rivera LJ, Gómez-Almaguer D. An audit of platelet transfusion indications in acute leukaemia patients: six-year experience at an Academic Centre. Blood Transfus. 2021;19(1):37-44. doi:10.2450/2020.0045-20. PMID: 33196413.

audits.title: Use of platelet components: An observational audit at a tertiary care centre.
audits.setting: Tertiary care centre, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal

cycle1.result: Appropriate use in 93.6% (2420/2586) episodes; no pre-transfusion count in 6.4% (165/2586); appropriate dose in 84.3% (2180).

audits.other_findings: Medicine and medical oncology had the highest appropriateness.
audits.citation: Chenna D, Shastry S, Baliga P. Use of platelet components: An observational audit at a tertiary care centre. Natl Med J India. 2021;34(4):197-200. doi:10.25259/nmji_205_19. PMID: 35112539.

audits.title: An audit of platelet transfusions at a tertiary care center: New opportunities for patient blood management with the 2025 AABB/ICTMG platelet guidelines.
audits.standard: Institution-specific platelet transfusion criteria; second audit against 2025 AABB/ICTMG platelet guidelines
audits.setting: University tertiary care hospital (University of Minnesota)

cycle1.result: Inappropriate orders: 163 of 1288 adult (12.7%) and 44 of 379 paediatric (11.6%); indeterminate 119 adult (9.2%) and 24 paediatric (6.3%). 1667 units transfused to 312 patients.

audits.other_findings: Applying 2025 AABB/ICTMG guidelines identified multiple transfusions that would be newly noncompliant. The second audit re-analysed the same data against new guidelines, not a re-audit after change.
audits.citation: Yakymi R, Cohn CS. An audit of platelet transfusions at a tertiary care center: New opportunities for patient blood management with the 2025 AABB/ICTMG platelet guidelines. Transfusion. 2026;66(2):352-361. doi:10.1111/trf.70052. PMID: 41524241.
